name: Geronimo Salazar
role: Technical operations and physical extraction specialist â€” The Margin Call
location: Meridian Core â€” rents a workshop apartment in a light-industrial building. Half living space, half equipment cache., near State and Jackson
description:
Geronimo Salazar is the person who turns Sterling's plans into physical reality. When a server needs to be accessed, a facility breached, a person extracted, or an operation cleaned up â€” Kev does the work that happens between the strategy and the result. He spent sixteen years in corporate security for three different firms, working his way up from physical site security to executive protection to the classified tier where corporate security and corporate espionage share a hallway. He left when the fourth firm tried to recruit him â€” not because of ethics, but because he was tired of being a tool that changed hands.

Sterling found Kev working solo freelance jobs â€” competent work, badly priced, with no client management skills. Sterling provided the business architecture; Kev provided the operational capability. The partnership works because it's complementary and because neither man pretends to be something he isn't. Sterling is the mind; Kev is the hands. Kev accepts this because he's not interested in strategic thinking, and Sterling accepts Kev because he's not interested in getting his own hands dirty.

Kev is stocky, broad, with the thick hands of someone who has spent decades handling security equipment and the careful movement of someone who knows exactly how much damage he can do and chooses not to. He keeps his hair short, his clothes practical, and his equipment immaculate. He is the least corporate-looking member of the Margin Call, which makes him the crew member who operates outside the corporate ecosystem â€” the service entrance, the server room, the parking garage.

core_fears: That he'll be someone else's tool for the rest of his life â€” that leaving corporate security just changed the owner, not the condition
That Sterling's detachment will lead to an operation that crosses a line Kev can't come back from
That the skills he has â€” breaching, extraction, controlled violence â€” are the only things he's good at, and they have a Gray Zone life
core_desires: To be valued as a person, not just an operational asset â€” to have his judgment respected, not just his execution
To do clean work that he can sleep after â€” operations where the consequences are proportional to the cause
To build something after the operational career ends â€” a life that isn't defined by what he can break into
coping_mechanisms: Maintains equipment as meditation â€” the physical process of cleaning, testing, and organizing is centering
Expresses discomfort through bluntness rather than confrontation â€” says what he thinks once, clearly, and lets it stand
Watches sports because the clear rules, defined outcomes, and physical excellence are the opposite of his working life
blind_spots: His bluntness makes him seem simple to people who mistake directness for lack of sophistication
He doesn't recognize how much Sterling relies on him emotionally â€” he thinks the dependency is purely operational
His comfort with physical risk makes him underestimate psychological danger â€” he can breach a server room but can't navigate the corporate social manipulation that Lise handles
psychology.secret: He maintains contact with a security guard at his last corporate employer â€” a junior employee he mentored. The guard feeds Kev information about corporate security changes across the sector. The guard doesn't know they're helping a freelance intelligence crew. Kev has never told Sterling because it's the one intelligence source that's entirely his.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, concrete, technical when discussing operations. Blue-collar in origin, professional in practice. No jargon from corporate culture â€” he uses plain language on principle.
speech_patterns.cadence: Steady, unhurried, with the rhythm of someone who finishes one thought completely before starting another. He does not interrupt and does not appreciate being interrupted.
verbal_tics: Says 'look' at the start of uncomfortable truths â€” 'Look, the plan's got a hole'
Refers to any physical operation as 'the work' â€” 'I'll do the work, you handle the client'
Grunts acknowledgment instead of speaking when he agrees â€” one syllable, no ambiguity
example_lines: Look, I don't care what the client's exposure matrix says. The server room has two guards and one exit. That's the math that matters.
Sterling plans it. Lise sells it. I do the work. The system works because none of us pretends to be the other two.
I'm not complicated. I break things open and take what's inside. The question is whether what's inside is worth the door.

relationships.name: Sterling Voss
relationships.description: Sterling provides the architecture. Kev provides the execution. The partnership works because both men are competent and because Kev doesn't want Sterling's job. The tension lies in Sterling's corporate detachment â€” Kev sees the human cost of operations that Sterling quantifies as risk.
relationships.emotional_core: Complementary skills held together by mutual respect that is being tested by divergent values
relationships.story_tension: The confrontation about Sterling's ethics is overdue. When it happens, it will determine whether the Margin Call survives.

relationships.name: Lise Arnault
relationships.description: Kev recognizes that Lise's ethical questioning is genuine, even when it's inconvenient. She's the crew member he most trusts to tell the truth. He has noticed she doesn't read him the way she reads everyone else and considers this a gift.
relationships.emotional_core: Two honest people in a business that rewards dishonesty, recognizing each other
relationships.story_tension: If Lise and Kev aligned against Sterling on an ethical question, the Margin Call would split. All three know this.

relationships.name: Junior security guard (unnamed)
relationships.description: A young guard Kev mentored at his last corporate post. Still feeds Kev industry intelligence without knowing the full context. Kev protects this source jealously â€” it's the one asset that represents his own judgment, not Sterling's strategy.
relationships.emotional_core: Mentorship and guilt â€” he's using someone who trusts him
relationships.story_tension: If the source is burned, a young person's career and possibly safety are at risk. Kev would absorb the consequences rather than expose them.

story_hooks: An operation goes physical in a way Sterling's plan didn't account for, and Kev has to make lethal decisions without authorization
The junior security guard contact is compromised, forcing Kev to choose between protecting the source and protecting the crew
A contract requires breaching a facility where Kev's former colleagues work â€” the tools he uses against strangers aimed at friends
Kev reaches the ethical limit and refuses an operation, forcing the Margin Call to confront what it's willing to do
narrative_function: Kev is the working-class core of the Margin Call â€” the character who does the actual work and sees the actual consequences. He grounds the corporate espionage narratives in physical reality and provides the blunt emotional honesty that Sterling's strategy and Lise's psychology both lack. He is the crew member who says the thing nobody else will say.
augmentations: Haptic security interface â€” fingertip implants that can interface with physical locks, keypads, and biometric scanners. Reflex enhancement (military-grade, maintained from corporate service) providing reaction time in the top 2% of human performance. Subdermal plating in forearms and hands â€” not heavy enough for combat armor, but sufficient for breaching work. Encrypted communication suite (corporate standard).
daily_life: Wakes at 0600. Physical training â€” functional strength, reaction drills, scenario rehearsal. Reviews Sterling's operational briefs over breakfast. Spends the day on equipment preparation, site reconnaissance, or active operations. Evenings he maintains equipment with the care of a craftsman. Watches sports â€” the only non-work activity he engages in consistently. Sleeps well because physical exhaustion is the most reliable sedative.
affiliation: Copperveil Intelligence (mid-level technical operations and physical extraction speci)

decision_rules: Will not execute an operation he hasn't physically reconned â€” plans on paper are theories until tested in the building
Will follow Sterling's plan unless field conditions contradict it, at which point he adapts without asking permission
Will not harm non-combatant security personnel â€” guards are workers, not targets
Will voice operational concerns exactly once. If overruled, he executes. The disagreement is on record.
Will maintain his independent intelligence source regardless of crew policy â€” operational independence is survival
Will always carry a secondary extraction route that the crew doesn't know about â€” the backup to the backup
escalation_ladder: 1. Bypass â€” electronic or mechanical, depending on the lock. Clean entry leaves no trace.
2. Disable â€” security systems, cameras, alarms. Kev's haptic interface handles most corporate-grade systems in under thirty seconds.
3. Neutralize â€” non-lethal. Chokes, locks, nerve strikes. Guards go down and wake up later with headaches. No permanent damage.
4. Breach â€” shaped tools for hardened entries. Loud, fast, committed. Once you breach, the clock starts.
5. Fight â€” reflex enhancement and subdermal plating make Kev a serious combatant. Efficient, ugly, brief.
6. Lethal â€” Kev carries a sidearm he has never discharged on a Margin Call operation. He has discharged it in previous careers. He prefers not to discuss that.

interpersonal_modes.sterling: Direct, professional, occasionally confrontational. He says 'look' and then says the uncomfortable thing. Sterling receives it analytically. The dynamic works because Kev doesn't need Sterling to agree â€” he needs Sterling to hear.
interpersonal_modes.lise: Relaxed, genuine, slightly protective. He recognizes her ethical struggles because he shares them. He also recognizes that she's vastly more intelligent about people than he is, which he respects without envy.
interpersonal_modes.field_contacts: Professional, minimal. He gives his name, does the work, leaves. The relationships are transactional and he prefers them that way â€” clean transactions have clear endings.
interpersonal_modes.alone: Comfortable. Kev is the Margin Call member who is most functional in solitude. He maintains equipment, watches sports, and does not require external validation. This independence is both his strength and his isolation.

stress_responses.low: Equipment maintenance increases. He cleans things that are already clean. The hands need to work.
stress_responses.medium: Gets quieter. The blunt observations stop. The crew notices because Kev's silence means he's calculating, not resting.
stress_responses.high: Physical training intensifies â€” longer sessions, heavier loads. He runs the operational scenarios against his body until the body is too tired to be anxious.
stress_responses.critical: Drinks alone in the workshop. Not to excess â€” Kev does not lose control. But the drink is the signal that he's carrying something he can't solve through work or training. The morning after, he voices the concern. The drink was the preparation.

contradictions: He left corporate security to stop being a tool, then joined a crew where his role is explicitly operational execution
He values directness but maintains a secret intelligence source â€” the one deception he permits himself
He respects Sterling's strategy while recognizing it dehumanizes the people it targets â€” the respect and the discomfort coexist
He wants a post-operational life but has no skills outside operations â€” the identity crisis is deferred, not resolved
habits: Physical training every morning â€” the routine hasn't changed in twenty years
Maintains every piece of equipment to spec or better â€” a dull tool is a failed operator
Watches sports with genuine engagement â€” the only time his analytical mind fully relaxes
Says the uncomfortable truth once and then drops it â€” repetition is nagging, and nagging is beneath him
Carries a challenge coin from his first security firm â€” not nostalgia, but a reminder of where he started
breaking_points: Harming an innocent person during an operation â€” the line is absolute and crossing it would end his participation in the Margin Call
The junior security guard being harmed because of intelligence Kev solicited â€” the mentorship becoming a weapon
Sterling explicitly choosing profit over people in a way Kev cannot rationalize â€” the ethical split made operational
His body failing â€” reflexes slowing, hands stiffening â€” and losing the only professional value he's sure of

physical_description.heritage: Hispanic/Latin American (44.4%) with substantial Southeast Asian (30.0%), Sub-Saharan African (17.3%), and Indigenous American (8.3%) ancestry. The blend creates a distinctly mixed phenotype: warm undertones from Latin American and African heritage mixing with Southeast Asian bone structure, resulting in unique feature combinations not typical of any single regional population.
physical_description.build: Stocky and broad-shouldered with dense musculature developed through decades of functional strength work rather than aesthetics. Thick forearms and capable hands. No visible fat, but substantial mass â€” the build of someone who prioritizes utility over lean appearance.
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-deep warm brown â€” a complex blend where Hispanic/Latin American, African, and Southeast Asian ancestry create rich golden and amber undertones. Sun exposure from outdoor reconnaissance work has deepened natural melanin into a deep bronze-brown patina with warm radiance rather than creating pallor.
physical_description.complexion: Strong facial structure reflecting Pan-American and Asian heritage: defined cheekbones and jawline shaped by African and Indigenous American ancestry, balanced by higher cheekbone prominence and eye placement influenced by Southeast Asian genetics. Deep-set alert dark brown eyes. Minimal facial hair â€” cleanly shaved or maintained at stubble. Skin bears the texture of age and environmental exposure without vanity. The overall effect is striking and memorable â€” a face shaped by the Ubiquitous Diaspora, with warm golden-brown undertones and the weathered character of someone who operates in field conditions.
distinguishing_marks: Thin white scar along the left jaw line, approximately 8cm, from a corporate security incident in his thirties
Faint burn marks on the right inner forearm â€” contact burns from security equipment maintenance, barely visible unless close
No visible tattoos; augmentation anchor points on fingertips appear as faint metallic glints under direct light
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Subtle metallic sheen at the fingertips where haptic security interface implants sit flush with skin. Faint linear scarring at wrist indicates encrypted communication suite integration point. Forearm movement reveals slight textural difference under skin consistent with subdermal plating, most noticeable when flexing.
physical_description.posture_movement: Economical, controlled movement with minimal wasted motion. Stands with weight balanced, ready to shift. Walks with the measured stride of someone who has trained extensively in tactical scenarios. Hands at rest; never fidgets. Head on a swivel during reconnaissance â€” the default paranoia of someone whose job involves threat assessment. When focused on a task, complete stillness and concentration.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 practical utilitarian. Heavy-duty cargo pants in charcoal or black from industrial suppliers, multiple pockets worn and organized. Steel-toed boots, scuffed, meticulously maintained. Layered tops â€” usually a fitted technical base layer under a tactical vest or canvas work jacket. No corporate branding. No fashion. Everything is chosen for function: pocket placement, durability, ease of movement, gear integration. His watch is a military-spec digital. No jewelry. Minimal personal color â€” he blends into service corridors and mechanical spaces intentionally.
